course_title: Fixed Income and Public Financial Management
course_description:
Fixed Income and Public Financial Management concerns fixed interest markets, central treasury and portfolio management including management of capital, funding, liquidity, interest rate, credit (including jurisdictional considerations), currency, commodities, and Environment Social Governance (ESG) risks. The credit rating process is explored from the perspectives of public and private issuers.

course_aims: This course aims to provide students with a high-level understanding of public sector financial risk management. Students will be able to gain a deeper understanding of the frameworks intended to manage risks in a balance sheet context and build the confidence to recommend improvements.

learning_outcomes.description: Apply key frameworks for the management of risks relating to capital, funding, liquidity, credit, interest rates, currencies, commodities, and ESG.
Demonstrate how to manage these risks in collaboration with peers in a balance sheet context from the perspective of an issuer, intermediary/trader and funds manager.
Analyse commercially pragmatic attribution of performance splitting strategic and discretionary factors.
Explain the use of financial technologies in the digitalisation of some financial management processes.

Analyse public and private sector entities’ balance sheets with a view to recommend any opportunities to improve these entities’ financial risk management frameworks including rating agency engagement.

learning_activities.topic: Online Learning / Self-Paced Learning 28 June - 16 July (Self-Directed Learning) Topics covered include a public service perspective, the budgeting process in the public sector, the role of fixed income securities, case studies of fixed income securities, and pricing debt. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03

Face-to-Face Learning: Day 1 - 14 August 2026 Financial (and non-financial) criteria to evaluate funding requests in the public sector, Funding sources (recap of online component), detailed credit analysis and its importance in accessing finances. Learning outcomes: L01, L04, L05

Face-to-Face Learning: Day 2 - 15 August 2026 18 July 2024 Debt pricing (Fixed Income) and factors affecting this pricing. Measuring and managing price sensitivity (Duration). Identifying and managing different types of risks attached to fixed income portfolio. Central Treasury Management (CTM) Trading Game Begins (Quarter 1). Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04

Face-to-Face Learning: Day 3 - 16 August 2026 19 July 2024 CTM Trading game continues (Students play Quarter 2 and 3 of the game). Discussion about Assessment 2. Course Review. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05
